text:
The Ducks came into Wednesday with four straight losses, Leo Carlsson day-to-day with an upper-body injury and Beckett Sennecke on injured reserve. They left with a 7-0 win over San Jose, their best night in weeks, and it came with a warning label attached: by expected goals (our measure of chance quality) this was a dead-even game, 2.35 for the Sharks and 2.28 for Anaheim. By our replays of every shot, San Jose deserved to win 51% of the time.

What separated the teams was finishing and goaltending, all of it at once. Anaheim scored three times in 1:40 late in the first. Judd Caulfield opened it at 13:37, Alex Killorn batted one in 30 seconds later, and Cutter Gauthier, chasing a scoring mark and the Rocket Richard race all month, snapped in a power-play goal at 15:17. Ian Moore made it 4-0 in the second on a chance our model rated under 1%, the least likely goal of the night, and Roger McQueen followed with a backhand set up by Nico Myatovic. Myatovic, recalled when Sennecke went on IR, picked up his first NHL point. Frank Vatrano and Killorn, with his second, finished it in the third. Mikael Granlund had three assists.

Laurent Brossoit was the other half of it. He stopped all 23 shots, 2.35 goals better than the chances deserved, including Tyler Toffoli's 21% look in the second, the best San Jose chance of the night. Brossoit got here the long way: a 164th overall pick in 2011 whose last stop before the NHL was the ECHL in Alaska. Both Lukas Dostal and Ville Husso have struggled over their last five starts, so a clean night from the third option matters.

At the other end, Alex Nedeljkovic allowed seven on 30 shots, 4.72 more than the chances deserved. That is a goaltending night, not a referendum on the Sharks' process. San Jose, already without Kiefer Sherwood, will want to forget it quickly. Toffoli plays his 1,000th NHL game at Madison Square Garden next Thursday, per Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest, which is a better thing to think about.
headline: Ducks end a winless week with a seven-goal night
